brief: A bracket to hang my 40-inch TV on the living room wall.

requirements.evidence: 3x full bases (-1,0,0; 0,0,0; 1,0,0) joint-bolted + locked, with 3x hex-acc-keyhole hangers on one face; check_build ok, meshClash clear. Shape allows lift-and-drop onto wall screws, but holding strength, screw pull-out, and wall suitability are not checked by the configurator.
No VESA interface, TV bolt pattern, tilt/arm, or 40-inch span verification exists in the catalog; only a 3-cell wide (~570mm) keyhole plate was built and no TV prop exists to stage it.

Parts are 3D printed in a user-chosen material; configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about material strength, load ratings, creep, heat or wall fixings. A heavy TV must not be hung on printed plastic without rated hardware and structural advice.
requirements.requirement: Support TV weight safely and reliably

finish.summary: Built a small keyhole-hanger wall plate mock-up (3 bases + 3 keyholes, locked and capped, clash-clear) to show the mounting idea, but it is not a rated TV bracket: safe support of a 40-inch TV is unmet — use a commercial steel VESA wall mount into studs/masonry.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: This calls for strength and wall-anchoring I can't verify in plastic — I'll still mock up the bracket shape to show the limits.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A side connector joins two bases that stand side by side on the same storey. Bases that touch with no connector on the wall between them are one body (joint bolts); every wall between two groups needs a connector, walls inside a group stay bare. get_build lists each touching wall and the groups. parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: L bracket
parts.use: Back plate on the flat, shelf on top, gusset underneath: the part to bolt on when something has to stick out sideways and stay level.
